Triage (central triage seat, daily round 2026-08-27, session `session_01Czs5tCwMymUvzB9QCA2yhH`): routed `domain:ui`, type **Task**. Rationale: the two honest routes both land in objectui's publish surfaces (README + the `AuthoredColumnOverrides` held band at PR #6590's keyhole) — release-library face, ui execution seat per the three-way split. The card already carries the maintainer's startup-stage rule (2026-08-27): with no measured demand, remove/withdraw is the lean default; enforce only on a measured authoring story, and stop-and-report if enforcing would widen behaviour beyond the documented override.

PM note from #6625's implementation (PR #6636) — a fold into that PR was considered and **correctly declined**. Recording it so the next person to pick this card up has the analysis rather than re-deriving it.

**Mechanically it folds.** `FieldMeta.referenceTo` is written-never-read on that path by the same evidence shape as `decimals` (`LookupCellRenderer` resolves `reference_to` / `reference`; `computeLookupExpand` reads the object schema). It sits in the same type, and removing it hits the **same coupling** — it would drop out of `EnrichedColumn`'s write-side tombstone band, so it needs the identical hand-written tombstone, roughly fifteen lines next to the one PR #6636 adds.

**Decisionally it does not.** This card is enforce-or-remove with **two** live branches — fix the spelling chain so the README promise becomes real, or withdraw the README line — and only one of them is a removal. Folding it into a retirement PR would have silently picked the withdraw branch, which is precisely the ruling this card exists to obtain. The dev stopped at exactly the right place and said what it would need: a ruling that this card takes the **withdraw** branch.

⛔ I am not making that call from this seat, and neither should the next execution seat. It decides whether a documented, published promise becomes real or is retracted, which is not a mechanical edit.

**What is now cheaper than it was**, if the withdraw branch is ever ruled: PR #6636 establishes the exact pattern and the precedent in the same file. The tombstone would be a sibling of `ObjectDataTableRetiredDecimalsTombstone`, for the same reason, in the same seam.

**And one measured fact that changes this card's framing** — it is not a published-type question. `FieldMeta` is **not** re-exported by `plugin-dashboard`'s barrel, and the package's `exports` map publishes only the root entry, so no consumer can name the type. Whatever is decided here, it is a package-internal contract change plus a README correction — not a removal from a published type surface. (Note this also corrects the framing in my own #6625 dispatch order, which called it "removing members from a published type". It isn't, and the dev measured that rather than accepting my wording.)

**Standing hazard for whoever implements either branch**, learned from #6636 and worth stating on this card because it applies to both: this repo has **two** seam bands derived from `keyof FieldMeta` — `EnrichedColumn`'s write-side tombstones (#6373) and `AuthoredColumnOverrides`' read-side band (#6425). A fence naming only one under-describes the blast radius of touching any member. My #6625 order named only one; the dev found the second.

Evidence for this card's open ruling, gathered on #6528 and **reported rather than acted on** — that seat was explicitly barred from touching `plugin-dashboard` or `FieldMeta`, and nothing below settles this card.

**The spec's own position on the spelling, measured against `@objectstack/spec` 17.2.0:** `ObjectSchema.safeParse` **refuses `referenceTo` by name** on a `FieldSchema`, with an explicit rename hint to `reference`, and the alias table folds `relatedTo` / `referenceTo` / `target` / `targetObject` / `lookupObject` onto `reference` — never the reverse. So on the wire, the canonical spelling is settled and this one is rejected.

⚠️ **The trap for whoever implements either branch here, and it is a grep trap.** In this repo `referenceTo` also survives **legitimately as an internal TypeScript property name** — `DatasetRelationship.referenceTo` (which is a resolver's *output*, not an input) and `plugin-dashboard`'s own `FieldMeta.referenceTo`, which is this card's subject. Those are not wire keys, and a census that greps the identifier will conflate the two populations and over-count the evidence in whichever direction it is already leaning.

The #6528 census kept them apart deliberately, and its own numbers show why it matters: of 360 lookup/master_detail defs in this tree, the `reference_to` bulk belongs to **ObjectUI's own view/field schema — a different contract** that `plugin-detail` translates *into* from the served `reference`, not to the object-metadata surface at all.

**What this does and does not do for the fork here.** It strengthens the case that the *wire* spelling is decided, so a README promise phrased around `referenceTo` is documenting something the spec rejects. It says nothing about whether `FieldMeta.referenceTo` — an internal member with no wire exposure — should be made real or withdrawn. That is still the ruling this card waits on, and it is still not this seat's to make.

Related, and the reason the platform-wide question may be worth settling first: #6528's dev also found that objectstack's public-form lookup-picker route keeps its **own** legacy-spelling chain, with a test asserting that *"stored pre-fold rows are live data, not history"*. That is the strongest surviving argument that stored legacy rows exist at all, and it sits one repo over from three consumers that have now removed their leniency. Filed separately so the platform's stance lives in one place rather than being re-decided per consumer.

Claim: `domain:ui` @ objectui PM seat, session `8ca04858-ea8e-5b85-9182-de59aa49e00c` — branch `claude/issue-6597-referenceto-enforce-or-remove`.

## ⛔ Revising my own note of 2026-08-28T07:40Z, and saying why

That comment said: *"I am not making that call from this seat, and neither should the next execution seat."* I am dispatching this card, so I owe the reason rather than quietly contradicting myself.

That note was written about **folding this card into PR #6636**, where folding would have silently picked the withdraw branch **without measuring** — which is the one thing the card exists to prevent. Declining that was right and stays right.

But re-reading the card as a whole: the maintainer **already supplied the decision rule**, in the card's own body and repeated by triage —

> Under the maintainer's standing startup-stage rule (2026-08-27: deprecated/alias spellings retire immediately, no transition windows), **this is the lean default when no demand is measured**.
> …**enforce only on a measured authoring story**, and stop-and-report if enforcing would widen behaviour beyond the documented override.

⇒ That is a **conditional disposition**, not an open fork. What is missing is not a ruling — it is **the measurement nobody has taken**. So this dispatches as a measure-then-act card with the maintainer's own conditional as its decision procedure, and the stop-and-report preserved intact.

⭐ Lane rule this pins down, and it is the mirror of the one that paid out four times today: reading the thread to the end can also tell you a card is **more** dispatchable than a prior note claimed, not only less. The prior note is evidence about the moment it was written.

## The evidence already on this card — ⛔ do not re-derive it

- **The spec has settled the wire spelling.** Against `@objectstack/spec` 17.2.0, `ObjectSchema.safeParse` **refuses `referenceTo` by name** on a `FieldSchema` with a rename hint to `reference`, and the alias table folds `relatedTo` / `referenceTo` / `target` / `targetObject` / `lookupObject` **onto** `reference`, never the reverse. So a README line phrased around `referenceTo` documents something the spec rejects.
- ⚠️ **`FieldMeta` is NOT a published surface.** It is not re-exported by `plugin-dashboard`'s barrel and the package's `exports` map publishes only the root entry, so no consumer can name the type. This is a **package-internal contract change plus a README correction** — ⛔ not a removal from a published type surface. (This also corrects my own #6625 dispatch order, which called it that. It isn't, and a dev measured it rather than accepting my wording.)

## ⚠️ Two traps that have already caught people on this key

1. ⛔ **`referenceTo` is a grep trap.** It survives **legitimately** as an internal TypeScript property name — `DatasetRelationship.referenceTo` (a resolver's *output*, not an input) and `plugin-dashboard`'s own `FieldMeta.referenceTo`, this card's subject. Those are not wire keys. **A census that greps the identifier conflates two populations and over-counts in whichever direction it is already leaning.** Keep them apart deliberately, and report the split.
2. ⛔ **There are TWO seam bands derived from `keyof FieldMeta`** — `EnrichedColumn`'s write-side tombstone band (#6373) and `AuthoredColumnOverrides`' read-side band (#6425). A fence naming only one **under-describes the blast radius** of touching any member. My #6625 order named only one; the dev found the second. Both are in scope for this card's fence.

## What is cheaper than it was

If the measurement lands on withdraw, PR #6636 established the exact tombstone pattern in the same seam — the new one is a sibling of `ObjectDataTableRetiredDecimalsTombstone`, for the same reason, roughly fifteen lines. ⛔ That does not pre-decide the branch; it means the withdraw branch is now cheap, not that it is chosen.

Surface is free as of 15:07Z — #6686 landed and released `packages/plugin-grid` / `packages/types`.

ACCEPT — PR #6695, head `3c5d330a8`, flipped ready; auto-merge once its table is green.

## The measurement was taken, and it is what picked the branch

This was dispatched as a measure-then-act card precisely so the branch would not be chosen by default. The demand census came back **zero on every path**, and it is reported per-path rather than as a total:

- `LookupCellRenderer` resolves `reference_to` / `reference` — **never** `referenceTo`;
- `computeLookupExpand` builds `$expand` from the **schema**, never from an authored key;
- `RecordDetailDrawer` **never offers a column override at all**;
- `ObjectGrid`'s sibling relational-meta pass-through copies only from the schema field def;
- no doc, example or fixture shows the pattern.

⇒ No measured authoring story ⇒ the maintainer's standing startup-stage rule selects **withdraw**. ⭐ That is the rule doing the deciding, which is exactly why the card was dispatched rather than escalated again.

## ⛔ And the withdrawal is a DECLARED refusal, at both bands

`FieldMeta.referenceTo` is retired, the README line is withdrawn, and the refusal is re-stated by hand at **both** `keyof FieldMeta` seam bands — `EnrichedColumn`'s write-side tombstones **and** `AuthoredColumnOverrides`' read-side band — via `ObjectDataTableRetiredReferenceToTombstone`, the exact sibling of #6625's decimals tombstone.

That second band is the one my own earlier dispatch order under-described, and it was in this card's fence for exactly that reason. Both were hit.

⭐ The ablation proves the tombstone bites in the only way that works: removing the intersection turns two `@ts-expect-error` directives **unused**, and `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` exits 2 naming exactly those two lines. **TS2578 is the instrument** — a green test run would have shown nothing, because the directives are erased before vitest sees them. Mutation confirmed on disk by `grep -c` on the tombstone identifier (7 → 0) plus a marker; restore verified with `git diff HEAD --quiet` and a clean re-run.

⭐ Lint narrowing proved rather than asserted: 0 errors, 59 warnings — and the 59 was **measured identical to the `origin/main` baseline for the same four files via `eslint --stdin`**, so **0 new**. Comparing against the baseline instead of just reporting a count is what makes "no regression" a measurement.

⚠️ `check:readme-exports` reported **NOT MEASURED** — population collapsed, 13 against a floor of 25, because sibling packages' `dist/` are unbuilt in a fresh worktree. Reported in those words, with the relevant sub-fact stated: `plugin-dashboard`'s own README raised zero findings. ⛔ Neither green nor red.

And the branch was **merged onto current `main` and re-verified** after my nudge — a green measured against a 40-minute-old base is not a green against what lands.

## ⭐⭐ The out-of-scope finding is bigger than the card

**#6694**: `ObjectDataTable` and `RecordDetailDrawer` **never feed `reference_to` / `reference` onto `FieldMeta` at all**. So `useRefObjectSchema`-driven display-name resolution and `ReferencedRecordLink`'s drill-through links **silently never engage for any lookup cell in either widget**. `ObjectGrid`'s `applyRelationalMeta` is the working sibling that shows what it should look like.

⇒ That is a whole capability quietly inert in two widgets — and it is the *reason* the census found zero readers, not merely a neighbour of it. The dev correctly identified it as a **behaviour change, not a retirement**, put it outside this card's stop-and-report line, and filed it unassigned with a `finding` label rather than widening. Exactly right: fixing it here would have turned a withdrawal into a feature restoration under a card that was chartered to measure demand.

⭐ Also handled well: a `PATH` placeholder in the report comment hit the sanitizer, and the dev re-posted a corrected comment and **named which one is authoritative** rather than leaving two versions with no ordering. That hazard has bitten this lane before, on a maintainer ruling.
